hazard: Continued prevalence of New Psychoactive Substances and inadequate staffing of Substance Misuse Team

concerns.quote: That there is no proper provision for the care and supervision of prisoners who present with complex physical and/or mental health needs
concerns.hazard: lack of proper care and supervision of prisoners with complex physical and mental health needs

concerns.quote: That at present, if a prisoner is assessed as needing a four person unlock, and is within the Segregation Unit, there are insufficient prison staff to provide him with a proper regime and to unlock him after lunchtime
concerns.hazard: insufficient prison staff to provide proper regime and unlock prisoners in segregation

concerns.quote: That the use of New Psychoactive Substances (NPS) remains rife within the prison, and presentations such as Mr [name redacted] are not diminishing, and that the Substance Misuse Team requires further staff to be effective in future
concerns.hazard: continued prevalence of New Psychoactive Substances and inadequate staffing of Substance Misuse Team

concerns.quote: That the documentary tool for decision making between prison staff and healthcare staff, as to whether a prisoner is fit to remain in Segregation and should do so, is unclear in design or in use
concerns.hazard: unclear documentary tool for decision making between prison staff and healthcare staff regarding segregation fitness

concerns.quote: That healthcare staff are insufficiently alert to the issue that physical symptoms which require urgent medical attention may be occluded by mental health issues
concerns.hazard: insufficient alertness of healthcare staff to physical symptoms occluded by mental health issues

concerns.quote: The existence of "confirmation bias" or "confirmatory bias" when dealing with detainees with a known history of recreational use of drugs in such a way that when a detainee presents in a manner that is interpreted as being presumed and/or assumed to be under the influence of drugs, this presumption and/or assumption is not challenged or tested or verified
concerns.hazard: presumption of drug influence not challenged

concerns.quote: Concerns of co-detainees are not appreciated or noted or actively sought

Record keeping and purported observations of detainees who are incapacitated by reason of presumed self-induced intoxication are inaccurate, irregular and unavailable for inspection by health care personnel
Discipline staff have no meaningful training on the categories of self-induced intoxication and in particular "new psychoactive substances" such as the synthetic cannabinoid known as "Spice
concerns.hazard: lack of training on new psychoactive substances

concerns.quote: There is no adequate communication or working protocols as between Discipline staff and healthcare staff for clear escalation pathways when dealing with a presumed "Spice" related incident

There is no adequate communication or working protocols as between Discipline staff and healthcare staff for clear escalation pathways when dealing with an incident that may have commenced as a drug related incident but develops into a potential medical emergency

links.explanation: Both reports highlight problems related to the prevalence and handling of new psychoactive substances (NPS) such as Spice within custodial settings. The earlier report calls for more substance‑misuse staff to address ongoing NPS use, while the later report points out that discipline staff lack meaningful training on these substances.
